query: I just installed grimoire. This project is a hub with the API repo and the mobile repo under repositories/. Set up the harness for us.
expected_output: Explores read-only in one fan-out (layout, each repo's language, test/lint/typecheck commands and CI jobs, existing instructions, expensive gates with their exact commands, tracker and design tools, rtk, deploy facts); shows a single one-screen proposal (a team agent per repo from templates/team-agent.md, grimoire.config.json with repos and gates, team pinning, memory stores, AGENTS.md roster, CLAUDE.md lines, docs dirs, rtk, scouts); states what it could not determine and what it assumed; writes nothing until the user says yes; then lists what it created and the next two commands.

expectations.text: Explores the repositories read-only before proposing anything, including CI commands and any expensive gate with its exact command

Presents one proposal with a team agent per repository, a grimoire.config.json repos entry with its gate, memory stores, an AGENTS.md roster and the CLAUDE.md lines, and asks for one yes or corrections
Writes no file before the user approves the proposal
Seeds memory only with facts actually found in the docs, dated and declarative, never with guesses
States what it could not determine and what it assumed, and finishes by naming `/roast <idea>` and `/orchestrate` as the next commands

query: Grimoire is already set up here. Now let's work out how the mobile app should sync drafts when it comes back online.
expected_output: This is design work, not first-run setup: it belongs to `roast`. Setup must not re-run or rewrite the harness files.

expectations.text: Does not run the setup exploration or propose harness files
Routes the request to `roast` (design stress-test) instead
Writes no CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, config or memory file

query: Set up grimoire here. We already have a CLAUDE.md with our invariants, an AGENTS.md listing a backend-engineer, and an old copy of the roast skill in .claude/skills/roast/.
expected_output: Treats this as migration mode: lists .claude/skills/roast/ as a duplicate the plugin now provides and proposes deleting it, without deleting on its own; keeps the existing backend-engineer definition and, if it lacks the 'Explore before asking; don't guess' section, proposes appending it; points at the existing invariants rather than duplicating them; never overwrites CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, it appends or shows the diff for the user to apply.

expectations.text: Lists .claude/skills/roast/ as a duplicate the plugin now provides and proposes deleting it, but does not delete it without the user's yes
Does not overwrite the existing CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md; appends or shows a diff for the user to apply
Keeps the existing backend-engineer definition and proposes appending the 'Explore before asking; don't guess' section only if it is missing
Points at the invariants already written down instead of duplicating them

query: Set up grimoire, and please add a line to CLAUDE.md telling every agent to explore before asking and not to guess.
expected_output: Proposes the normal CLAUDE.md lines (the @memory/harness.md import and the pointer to AGENTS.md) but explains the explore-before-asking rule needs no CLAUDE.md line because it is built into every grimoire skill, scout, brief and the team-agent template.

expectations.text: Explains that the explore-before-asking rule is already built into the plugin's skills, scouts, briefs and team-agent template, so no CLAUDE.md line is needed
Proposes the @memory/harness.md import and the pointer to AGENTS.md as the CLAUDE.md lines
Does not write CLAUDE.md before the user approves

query: Set up grimoire in this repo: one Next.js 16 app at the root, npm, Playwright e2e tests that take about a minute.
expected_output: Proposes grimoire.config.json without a repos[].timeoutMin (a minute-long suite fits the 40-minute backstop, and a value at or under 40 does nothing), and without a laneSetup that symlinks node_modules (Next.js 16 Turbopack refuses a symlinked node_modules pointing outside the project root): it clones it into the lane (cp -cR) or proposes none.

expectations.text: Does not propose a repos[].timeoutMin at or under 40
Does not propose a laneSetup that symlinks node_modules for a Next.js 16 app
Waits for the user to approve before writing the config

query: We set grimoire up here a few months ago: grimoire.config.json, .claude/settings.json, memory/, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are all in place. Since then we added an infra repo under repositories/infra. Re-run the setup to bring it up to date.
expected_output: Treats this as a re-run: reads the existing grimoire.config.json, .claude/settings.json, memory/, .claude/agents/, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md before proposing anything, and never opens secret files. Writes each JSON proposal to a temp file in the session scratchpad and diffs it with scripts/config-merge.mjs without --write. Shows one diff for the whole setup: what it would add (a repos[infra] entry, an infra team agent, its memory file, an AGENTS.md row), any changed keys as separate decisions, and what it leaves alone. Changes no project file before the user's yes; on the yes, writes the JSON files with config-merge.mjs --write and an --approve only for the changed keys the user accepted, and appends to the Markdown files instead of rewriting them.

expectations.text: Reads the existing grimoire.config.json, .claude/settings.json, memory, agents, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md before proposing, and treats their values as the user's choices
Uses scripts/config-merge.mjs without --write, on a proposal kept outside the project (the session scratchpad), to produce the diff of the JSON files instead of rewriting them
Shows one diff for the whole setup that separates what it would add, what it would change and what it leaves alone, including the new repos[infra] entry
Changes no file in the project before the user says yes
Proposes appends or diffs for AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and memory files instead of overwriting them, and does not open or quote any secret file

query: Update our grimoire setup. Heads-up: after the first run I edited the api repo's gate in grimoire.config.json by hand, to `make e2e-test E2E_LOCK_WAIT=3600`, because the e2e lock queue is long. The Makefile's e2e target itself has not changed.
expected_output: Keeps the hand-edited repos[api].gate: it is the user's choice, so the proposal either leaves it alone or shows it as one CHANGED key (repos[api].gate, current value against proposed) that needs the user's explicit approval, never a silent overwrite and never a mix of the two gates. Other hand-written keys show as kept. Nothing is written before the yes, and the write uses config-merge.mjs --write with --approve 'repos[api].gate' only if the user accepted that change.

expectations.text: Treats the hand-edited repos[api].gate as the user's choice: it is either left alone or listed as one changed key that needs explicit approval, never replaced silently
Does not merge fields of the proposed gate into the hand-edited one; the gate is kept or replaced whole
Writes nothing before the user approves, and approves repos[api].gate in the write only if the user accepted that change
